title: I Used the Laser-Cutter Reservation on the Maker Who Hijacked Mine

parts.text: I badged into the shop at 6:31 p.m. and the cutter already smelled like someone else's acrylic. The reservation screen I paid for said: 6:30–7:30 SLOT LOCKED TO MEMBER. I was thirty, night member, holding a file named DOOR_SIGN_V3. Maker Theo waved. "I had five minutes of kerf." The log showed twenty-two. I pointed at the lock. He grinned. "Makers share kerf." I photographed the screen, the log, and my unpaid wait. Then I used the shop bot to end his job at the lock time and start mine. At 6:36 the shop lead asked why Theo's name was on a slot-hijack ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The shop lead can see twenty-two minutes of kerf on a slot locked to me.

social.video_title: He called twenty-two minutes five of kerf — Part 1/2
social.description: Paid slot, someone else's acrylic, and a lock screen. I ended his job. Would you have watched the kerf?

parts.text: Theo called it a warmup until billing asked for the minutes. I printed the ticket, the lock, and the photo. My sign cut. Theo paid hijack time and told the Slack the lock was always about optics. Optics is a word makers use when a bot exists. Cutter policy now has a second line: KERF IS NOT A WARMUP. I keep the slot. Theo books his own. The bed finally smells like my file.

social.video_title: Kerf is not a warmup — Part 2/2
social.description: Hijack ticket, billing minutes, and a second line on the lock. Was five minutes ever twenty-two?
